ui_scope: Dedicated persistent celestial scene prototype: fixed Sun direction, time-driven Earth camera rotation, moving Moon, automatic close-up exit
ui_changes: portrait mode uses a horizontal glowing circular-thumb slider
landscape mode uses a vertical slider on the right side, with +12h at the top and −12h at the bottom to match upward-forward movement
slider input uses a fixed simulation anchor so drag values map consistently to time
Sun/Moon tracker icon starts inactive and panel stays closed on launch
controls remain above the bottom safe-area inset
changes: Selecting either Sun or Moon enters a shared Celestial View with both bodies visible.
Anchor the Sun direction and freeze Cesium lighting time at scene entry.
Rotate the camera around Earth’s polar axis as the ±12-hour time scroller changes to represent Earth rotation under fixed sunlight.
Update Moon direction and approximate phase from the selected simulation time.
Keep Celestial View active until the main Sun/Moon panel closes or zoom reaches the automatic Earth-view exit threshold.
Automatically exit Celestial View on close-up zoom while preserving the current close-up camera view.
Suppress the old blocky Moon visibility overlay while Celestial View is active.
Preserve existing HTML, CSS, base app, data store, Moon calculator, centred dock, and adaptive scroller.
Candidate requires iPhone/PWA visual and interaction testing; no runtime validation claim.
title: EARTH // LIVE — Celestial View Prototype v1.36
description: Introduces a dedicated Celestial View prototype with a fixed Sun direction, Earth rotation driven by the ±12-hour scroller, and a Moon that changes position with time. Both bodies remain visible while the Sun/Moon panel is open. Zooming close to Earth exits the celestial scene while preserving the close-up view. Existing layout and Earth assets are preserved. Requires iPhone/PWA testing; Moon model remains approximate.
